subject: Post-call: Private/VPC licensing & support options — follow-up and numbers
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call: Private/VPC licensing & support options — follow-up and numbers

Hi Sara — thanks again for the productive call earlier. Quick recap and the concrete asks we promised to follow up on. TL;DR below, full details and next steps after.

Recap (what we heard)
- Use case: clinical documentation augmentation and patient messaging across several internal apps.
- Initial monthly generation estimate: 8–12M tokens; peak/burst expected up to ~30M in some weeks.
- Must be deployed in a VPC with customer-managed networking and KMS. SOC2 evidence and audit logs required for procurement.
- Staging + Prod required; you may want a small Dev sandbox.

Asks we promised to answer (this email)
1) Licensing models and how unit economics map to target $/1M tokens.
2) Recommended environment count and support tiers.
3) Ballpark cost examples for your 10M token baseline + growth.
4) Next steps & attachments (draft terms + simple workbook).

Options (high level) — three typical private deployment paths we see:
A) Usage-first (metered) on private control plane — low upfront, per-1M token rate, infra pass-through. Good if you want minimal commit.
B) Reserved capacity (dedicated GPU pools) — monthly capacity fee (reserves cores/GPU hours) + discounted per-token overage. Predictable throughput and unit cost.
C) Enterprise license (flat platform fee) + per-environment add-ons — chosen when customers want unlimited-ish throughput and predictable billing for a portfolio of apps.

Ballpark unit economics (illustrative) — assume production inference with batching/caching applied. These are starting guidance ranges; final depends on quantization, model choice, and prefix cache hit-rate.
- Usage-first: $140–$220 per 1M tokens
- Reserved capacity: $60–$120 per 1M tokens (effective, after amortizing monthly capacity fee at 10–30M tokens/mo)
- Enterprise license: $35–$90 per 1M tokens (depends on committed capacity and term)

Example calc (10M tokens / mo baseline) — reserved capacity path:
- Reserved pool monthly fee (example): $18,000 (covers a mid-sized GPU pool)
- Estimated infra & runtime ops + token processing amortized: ~$8,000/mo
- Effective unit: (18,000 + 8,000) / 10 = $2,600 per 1M tokens — this is a raw example before discounts and optimization (we would push this down heavily through batching, quantization, and committing to a term).

Why that raw number looks high: the example above includes conservative pool sizing and no batching assumptions. With workload-aware batching, KV caching on prompts, and a 6–12 month commit we typically drive the effective $/1M token cost into the reserved capacity band above ($60–$120) for production workloads.

Environments & Support
- Recommended envs: Dev (sandbox), Staging (pre-prod), Production — total 3. Additional DR/Analytics envs billed as add-ons.
- Support tiers: Standard (business-hours, 24x5 monitoring, email support), Premium (24x7, 1-hour P1 response, named SE). Premium adds ~20–40% to platform fee depending on SLA and response commitments.

Attachments: I attached a short draft terms doc and a tiny workbook with the simple math (nimbus-maup-estimates.xlsx). I’ll also drop a HubSpot deal link in the thread.

Suggested next steps
- Confirm which licensing path you want us to price (Usage-first | Reserved | Enterprise).
- Confirm an expected baseline monthly token target you’re comfortable committing to for pricing (e.g., 10M / 20M / 30M).
- I’ll pull Marissa in to bake the formal quote and Marissa/Neha to confirm security and support SLAs.

Would you be able to confirm the baseline and preferred model by EOD Monday? If helpful, happy to share a quick one-page slide with comparative economics.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Sara — thanks, great questions. Below I laid out a concise worked example using reserved capacity assumptions and then the asks for approvals on pricing posture.

Worked example (reserved capacity, 10M tokens/mo baseline)
Assumptions:
- Model: quantized LLM variant (4-bit) with optimized kernels; average tokens per request = 300 tokens; KV cache hit-rate = 35% (prefix-heavy workload)
- Effective GPU footprint: pool sized for your peak concurrency, counts toward monthly fee
- Monthly pool fee (example quote-level): $12,000 — includes GPU runtime, monitoring, private control plane ops
- Ops & infra (network, storage, KMS ops): $4,000/mo
- Token processing variable: $2,000/mo (runtime per-token overhead after batching)

Total monthly = 12,000 + 4,000 + 2,000 = $18,000
Effective $/1M tokens = 18,000 / 10 = $1,800 per 1M tokens (raw)

Now the optimization steps we apply (typical on Day 1–90):
- Workload-aware batching & request shaping: reduces compute by ~25%
- Prefix/KV caching: effective token volume reduced ~20%
- Quantized model and kernel tuning: further 20% improvement in op cost
Compound effect: these combined often reduce the raw effective by ~70–80% in practice for production flows. Applying a conservative 75% improvement: 1,800 * 0.25 = $450 per 1M tokens. With a 12-month commitment and dedicated optimizations we routinely get into the $60–$120 band for many customers (larger scale and higher cache-hit-rate push lower).

Why the numbers vary widely: the biggest driver is cache-hit-rate and batching. For patient messaging with many templates, cache hits are high and your effective per-token cost will be materially lower.

Direct answer to your $80/1M target: yes, $80/1M is achievable for the reserved capacity path if:
- You commit to ~12–18 months and a baseline of 10–15M tokens/mo, and
- We apply the batching and KV caching optimizations and agree on a model variant that supports 4-bit quantization.

Support & SOC2 evidence
- Neha: can you confirm the SOC2 artifacts we can provide during procurement review (report, attestation, SOC2 controls mapping)? Also confirm timing for a signed Attestation letter.

Proposed commercial next steps (what I suggest we do now):
1) Redwood to produce a formal reserved-capacity quote with two tiers: (a) 12-month commit @ target $80/1M after optimizations (pilot discount for months 1–3), (b) 24-month commit with deeper discounts and reserved capacity sizing.
2) Share a technical onboarding plan (1–6 weeks) that documents caching, batching, and model tuning steps.
3) Procurement/legal to review the attached draft terms and send redlines.

Marissa — I’m proposing we position this as: pilot (3 months) at $120/1M effective + 12-month commit to reach $80/1M after optimizations. Approve to send quote?

Best,
Karthik
